summary: Two range towers that line up a dredged channel into Havre Boucher harbour, Nova Scotia: built 1878-79, kept mostly by the Webb family, now a steel front and a modular rear tower.

access.note: Site open, tower closed (Rowlett). The rear light stands on a hill above Highway 4 at the Havre Boucher exit. NSLPS lists the site as requiring a hike.

events.note: Station established, per Rowlett and the NSLPS rear list. The sources cited do not say what stood on the site then.
Tenders invited in 1878; the 1879 description says the two towers were erected in the past season.
Put in operation in October, per the 1879 description. Rowlett and the NSLPS give 1879.
Both towers stripped, shingled and given new sills.
Patrick Webb appointed keeper at Harbour au Bouche, 19 February 1896.
A new concrete foundation was poured for each tower.
Automation date per LighthouseFriends. The NSLPS dates the 1969 rear tower's automation to 1973.
NSLPS gives 1969 as the start of the third set of towers.
A coloured stripe was added to the seaward faces of the towers.
Rear tower replaced by a modular tower in March 2010. The front is now a skeletal steel tower.

corrections.why: The CCG list describes the front light as a square skeleton tower, and the NSLPS says the front tower is now a galvanized steel structure. The wood entry fits the 1879 tower, which Rowlett and the NSLPS say was replaced.

The CCG list (current edition) gives the rear light at 45 40 40.9 N, 061 31 42.7 W. The record's point is about 60 m from that position. The record's front position matches the CCG list to within about 20 m.

notes_for_editor: Dates in dispute: first light 1878 (the 1879 description, quoted by LighthouseFriends, says lit in October 'last') against 1879 (Rowlett; NSLPS). Rowlett and the NSLPS rear list also give 'station established 1842' and 'Began: 1842', which the sources cited do not explain; first_lit is set to 1878 but the 1842 date may be the station's earlier light. Automation: LighthouseFriends says 1963, NSLPS says the 1969 rear tower was automated by 1973. Tower replacement dates in the NSLPS list (1941-1954, 1945, 1969) do not match LighthouseFriends (1954 foundations only). Rowlett gives the 1879 front as 9 m (29 ft) against 32 ft in the 1879 description; the rear is 33 m focal height in Rowlett, 32.4 m in the CCG list and about 107 ft (32.6 m) in the 1879 description. The rear distance is 435 m in Rowlett and 433.2 m in the CCG list. The record's light.focal_height_m (8.3) and range (8) are the front light's values; the rear light's focal height (32.4 m, CCG) is not in the record. The record's status 'active' does not show that the CCG lists both lights as seasonal. OCR matching by column position: Patrick Webb's appointment (19 Feb 1896, scan p.233 / printed p.220 of the 1903 volume) and the 1907 list entry were matched by column position with 'Harbour au Bouche'; the 1906 list ('Harbour au Bouche Feb.') is consistent. Keepers Mary Webb (1896), Jeffrey T. Crispo (1916-1924) and Joseph K. Webb (1924-1963) appear only in LighthouseFriends; searches of the Marine corpus for Crispo found nothing, and the corpus ends in 1924. The 1879 description is second-hand (LighthouseFriends cites 'Annual Report of the Department of Marine and Fisheries, various years'); the 1879 volume is not in the corpus and archive.org search found no copy. LighthouseFriends is copyrighted: the story uses our own words and quotes from it only in the internal evidence. The LighthouseFriends name explanation (French 'blocked harbour', or Captain Francois Boucher wintering there in 1759) is unsourced and left out. Storms, wrecks and rescues: nothing tied to the range lights turned up in the corpus, Chronicling America ('Havre Boucher', 1880-1925, no hits), or the sources read; there is no storms chapter. An ARLHS entry, CAN-224 'Havre Boucher Outer Range Light' (lost, historic, approximately 45 41 N 61 32 W), is not in the record and was not researched; arlhs.com returned a certificate error, and the wlol.arlhs.com copy gives only the listing. The Lighthouse Digest database entry (access 'grounds only') returned HTTP 503 and was not used. novascotiavacation.ca is a generic tourist page with unreliable dates (for example, '1969' and 'since the mid-1800s') and was not used as a source. Checked on page images, 2026-10-28: the Patrick Webb row of the 1903 keeper list (Harbour au Bouche, appointed Feb. 19, 1896, salary $250) is printed p. 220 (scan p. 233). It was matched by column position in the OCR and confirmed on the image. The 1907 list line 'Webb, Patrick Harbour au Bouche' is printed p. 147 (scan 154). The 1914 'Havre bouche, range' entry is printed p. 58 (scan 65), per the corpus page lookup.
